headlines.description: Michael Carrick's future at Manchester United looks increasingly untenable after his side imploded in the second half to lose 2-0 against Chelsea.
headlines.shortLinkText: Carrick on the brink as Man Utd lose at Chelsea

events.name: Brighton & Hove Albion at Manchester City

headlines.description: Michael Carrick's future at Manchester United looks increasingly untenable after his side imploded in the second half to lose 2-0 against Chelsea.
headlines.shortLinkText: Carrick on the brink as Man Utd lose at Chelsea

events.name: Brighton & Hove Albion at Manchester City

headlines.description: Bournemouth boss Marco Rose was denied a first Premier League win after a calamitous goalkeeping mistake allowed Brentford to claim a 2-2 draw.
headlines.shortLinkText: Schade brace extends Bournemouth's winless run

headlines.description: Igor Jesus piled the misery on Aston Villa as his late goal snatched a 2-1 victory for Nottingham Forest at Villa Park.
headlines.shortLinkText: Late Forest winner piles misery on Aston Villa

headlines.description: Chelsea's chaotic start to life under Xabi Alonso continued with an entertaining 2-2 draw against Hull at Stamford Bridge.
headlines.shortLinkText: Chelsea draw with PL surprise package Hull City

headlines.description: Zian Flemming's first goal for Ipswich snatched a dramatic 3-2 victory at 10-man Crystal Palace for their second Premier League win of the season.
headlines.shortLinkText: Ipswich beat 10-man Palace with 90th-min winner

headlines.description: Fulham frustrated Liverpool to claim their first point of the season with a goalless draw at Anfield on Saturday.
headlines.shortLinkText: Liverpool held by out-of-form Fulham at Anfield

headlines.description: Tottenham Hotspur fired another blank after being frustrated by Everton in a 0-0 draw to extend their winless start to the new Premier League season to four matches.
headlines.shortLinkText: Winless Spurs still searching for 1st goal after Everton draw

headlines.description: Bruno Guimarães and Bukayo Saka helped maintain Arsenal's perfect start in the Premier League with a 2-0 win over Sunderland.
headlines.shortLinkText: Guimarães stunner helps Arsenal keep perfect start

events.name: Brighton & Hove Albion at Coventry City

headlines.description: Brighton dealt 10-man Coventry a crushing 5-0 defeat to condemn them to a fourth straight Premier League loss.
headlines.shortLinkText: Dunk screamer helps Brighton pile more PL misery on Lampard's Coventry

headlines.description: Erling Haaland secured Manchester City a memorable derby-day triumph as Manchester United failed to capitalise on Phil Foden's sending-off on a day of contentious decisions.
headlines.shortLinkText: Haaland goal decides VAR-heavy Manchester derby for 10-man City

headlines.description: Leeds sent sorry Newcastle spinning to a 4-1 defeat at Elland Road to extend their unbeaten Premier League start and climb to third in the table.
headlines.shortLinkText: Unbeaten Leeds cruise past Newcastle 4-1

headlines.description: Chelsea's winless run in the Premier League stretched to three matches as Brentford ran out deserved 3-0 winners at the Gtech Community Stadium.
headlines.shortLinkText: High-flying Brentford hammer struggling Chelsea

headlines.description: Aston Villa piled the pressure on big-spending Tottenham and Roberto De Zerbi with a 3-2 away victory to claim a first win in the Premier League this season.
headlines.shortLinkText: Drab Tottenham fall to Aston Villa defeat

headlines.description: Arsenal's 100% start to their Premier League title defence ended in emphatic fashion as Brighton secured a stunning 3-0 win against Mikel Arteta's dumbstruck side.
headlines.shortLinkText: Champions Arsenal battered by brilliant Brighton

headlines.description: Abdul Fatawu's dismissal after being shown a second yellow card for diving capped a frustrating afternoon for Ipswich in their 1-0 defeat at Everton.
headlines.shortLinkText: Barry strikes for Everton to sink 10-man Ipswich

headlines.description: Hull's unbeaten start to life in the Premier League came to an end with a 2-1 defeat to Newcastle at St James' Park.
headlines.shortLinkText: Newcastle strike early, end Hull's unbeaten record

headlines.description: Jay DaSilva fired Coventry to their first Premier League win in 25 years as they beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 in another game mired by VAR controversy.
headlines.shortLinkText: Coventry claim first PL win of season at Forest

headlines.description: Alexander Isak's second-half strike secured Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola all three points on his return to the Vitality Stadium in a 1-0 victory over his old club Bournemouth.
headlines.shortLinkText: Iraola's Liverpool triumph on Bournemouth return

headlines.description: Leeds and Crystal Palace battle to gritty goalless draw
headlines.shortLinkText: Leeds and Palace battle to gritty goalless draw

headlines.description: Brian Brobbey scored a hat trick in a losing cause as Manchester City maintained their 100% Premier League start with a frantic 5-3 win over Sunderland.
headlines.shortLinkText: Man City down Sunderland in eight-goal thriller

headlines.description: A comical own goal by Lisandro Martinez saw Manchester United fail to win for a third Premier League game in a row as they drew 1-1 with Fulham at Craven Cottage.
headlines.shortLinkText: Man United rescue draw at Fulham after own goal

headlines.description: Arsenal struck twice in eight second-half minutes to secure a comeback 2-1 win against Leeds at the Emirates Stadium and move level on points with Manchester City at the Premier League summit.
headlines.shortLinkText: Arsenal come from behind to overcome Leeds

headlines.description: Kristoffer Ajer's second-half equaliser ensured Brentford continued their unbeaten start to the Premier League season in an entertaining 2-2 draw at Aston Villa.
headlines.shortLinkText: Brentford stay unbeaten after compelling Villa draw

headlines.description: Jordan Henderson was the unlikely hero as Chelsea's entertainers blew Bournemouth away in a comprehensive and chaotic 5-1 win at Stamford Bridge.
headlines.shortLinkText: Henderson, 36, nets unlikely brace as Chelsea thrash B'mouth

headlines.description: Ipswich produced a dramatic turnaround to beat Fulham 2-1 after late goals by Abdoul Ouattara and Dara O'Shea extended Alvaro Arbeloa's winless start to six Premier League matches.
headlines.shortLinkText: Ipswich bag late dramatic victory against Fulham

headlines.description: Maxim De Cuyper and Jaouen Hadjam were both on the scoresheet as 10-man Brighton clinched a 2-0 win over Sunderland at the Stadium of Light.
headlines.shortLinkText: Brighton keep pressure on City, Arsenal with win

headlines.description: Dominic Solanke capitalised on weak Manchester United defending as winless Tottenham recovered from Rodrigo Bentancur's dismissal to snatch a late 1-1 draw as boos filled Old Trafford once again.
headlines.shortLinkText: Solanke rescues point for 10-man Spurs as hapless Man United flatter to deceive again

headlines.description: Crystal Palace dealt former boss Oliver Glasner a blow after they bounced back to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 on the Austrian's first return to Selhurst Park.
headlines.shortLinkText: Palace come from behind to beat Forest 3-1 and spoil Oliver Glasner's return to Selhurst Park

headlines.description: Hull retained their unbeaten home record since returning to the Premier League with an entertaining 2-2 draw against Everton at the MKM Stadium.
headlines.shortLinkText: Belloumi maintains Hull's unbeaten home record

headlines.description: Uncertainty may surround Manchester City's future but nothing changed for them on the pitch as the Premier League leaders successfully came through their first public examination since their guilty verdicts.
headlines.shortLinkText: Manchester City beat Liverpool with ease in first match after guilty verdicts

headlines.description: Coventry City picked up their first home victory in the Premier League for 25 years with an emphatic 4-1 win over Newcastle United on Monday.
headlines.shortLinkText: Coventry stun Newcastle with emphatic 4-1 win

article.story:
Hull's unbeaten start to life in the Premier League came to an end with a 2-1 defeat to Newcastle at St James' Park.

A pulsating opening saw Joe Willock and Lewis Hall score in the first seven minutes and the Magpies were unable to capitalise on another opportunity to inflict further misery on Hull before the break when Yoane Wissa's penalty was saved.

Substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho pulled one back for the Tigers, but Newcastle managed to withstand a late flurry of attacks from the visitors to seal victory, which comes only five days after a bruising 4-1 defeat to Leeds.

With an increasing injury list to contend with, Matthias Jaissle made two switches from the Leeds defeat as Sean Steur and Willock both started.

Hull also opted for two changes, with Lucas Herrington and Sorba Thomas lining up, the latter of whom was making his first Premier League start.

Willock made an instant impact on his return to the starting 11, having a shot blocked, and moments later sent the Magpies ahead with a low finish past Konstantinos Tzolakis from Harvey Barnes' ball.

Newcastle's ruthless start continued as they doubled their lead only four minutes later, with Barnes once again the provider this time for Hall, who dispatched the ball into the bottom right corner.

Hull began to see more of the ball as Mohamed Belloumi piled pressure on Lukás Hornícek and snatched the ball from his feet, but the goalkeeper recovered.

Matt Crooks' dangerous cross for Thomas was bundled behind for a corner, but the Magpies continued to threaten as Jacob Murphy dragged an effort wide.

The winger sent another shot past the upright and was in the thick of the action again, firing a teasing ball across the box towards Hall, who was unable to stab home.

Newcastle had the opportunity to extend their lead from the penalty spot before the break when Thomas made a grab at Murphy's foot and VAR upheld the onfield decision, but Wissa's spot-kick was pushed away by Tzolakis.

Thomas blasted an effort wide at the end of the half and Tzolakis was called into action after the restart to hold Sven Botman's header from Hall's cross.

Belloumi lifted the ball over the bar moments later and sent another effort over as Hull looked to strike.

- First-month grades for all 20 Premier League teams: A+ to F
- Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle hoping for 'positive' update on Anthony Elanga injury

The visitors pulled one back in the 67th minute when Belloumi threaded the ball in for Cho, who scored just four minutes after being introduced as his shot bounced off the post and into the net.

Hull continued to apply pressure when Hornicek parried away Belloumi's effort and following a string of chances aimed towards the Newcastle goal, Tim Iroegbunam sliced a shot narrowly wide of the post.

The momentum was fully with Hull in the final stages as Lucas Gourna-Douath's strike smashed into a crowded box and Joe Gelhardt chipped wide, but the Tynesiders held on.

article.headline: Man City down Sunderland in eight-goal thriller
article.description: Brian Brobbey scored a hat trick in a losing cause as Manchester City maintained their 100% Premier League start with a frantic 5-3 win over Sunderland.
article.linkText: Man City down Sunderland in eight-goal thriller

images.name: Manchester City score five in thrilling win over Sunderland
images.caption: The Sky Blues remain top of the Premier League table after a goal-filled 5-3 victory over the Black Cats.

article.story:
Brian Brobbey scored a hat trick in a losing cause as Manchester City maintained their 100% Premier League start with a frantic 5-3 win over Sunderland.

In a game characterized by poor defending, City struggled to slow down the fired-up visitors at the Etihad Stadium, with Brobbey a constant thorn in their side.

Ultimately two goals from Antoine Semenyo and a late strike from Erling Haaland finished the job for City, for whom Enzo Fernández and Rayan Cherki were also on target.

Unlike in last week's Manchester derby, City failed to assert control against a Sunderland side clearly not drained by its midweek Europa League excursions.

For new manager Enzo Maresca, however, it was a fifth successive league win and City head into the international break with a three-point lead at the top.

City were given an early warning as Sunderland broke from deep and Enzo Le Fée played in Nilson Angulo but he steered wide.

Sunderland paid for that miss as Fernandez fired home from a ninth-minute free kick after Iliman Ndiaye was brought down by Dayann Methalie.

Goalkeeper Robin Roefs left a huge gap at his near post having set up with only two men in the wall. Fernandez took full advantage, curling in his first goal since his £125 million move from Chelsea.

Sunderland responded quickly and were back level three minutes later as Lee played a superb ball between Rúben Dias and Matheus Nunes and Brobbey deftly flicked beyond Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Sunderland's good work up front contrasted with that at the back, as an attempt to play out plunged them into more trouble. Kevin Danso gifted possession and confusion reigned before Cherki tucked in.

Again City could not hang onto the lead as Le Fée played in Thomas Meunier and his square pass was turned in by Brobbey. The goal was awarded after a lengthy VAR check for offside, leaving Donnarumma to vent his anger at the standard of Cherki's defending.

City regained the lead before the break after a Cherki cross led to more panic in the Sunderland area. The Black Cats claimed Marc Guéhi handled but nothing was given and Semenyo lashed in.

Haaland should have had another but inexplicably missed an open goal after being teed up by Ndiaye and Brobbey was denied another when a shot took an awkward deflection and was palmed onto the bar by Donnarumma.

City's fourth came early in the second half as a Cherki pass intended for Haaland ricocheted off a defender and bobbled into the path of Semenyo. Again he finished clinically.

Yet still City were not convincing and more sloppy play allowed Sunderland back in.

Angulo brought down a long ball as he ran in at the back post and although his effort looked like it might cross the line, Brobbey took no chances and pounced to compete his treble.

Remarkably it could have been 4-4 moments later as Donnarumma failed to deal with a cross and the ball bounced off Dias toward goal. The Portuguese sprinted back to hook off the line.

Haaland finally put the result beyond doubt.

Making amends for his earlier miss, the Norwegian slid in at the back post to tap in after Josko Gvardiol broke clear down the left nine minutes from time.

article.headline: Leeds and Crystal Palace battle to gritty goalless draw
article.description: Leeds and Crystal Palace battle to gritty goalless draw
article.linkText: Leeds and Palace battle to gritty goalless draw
article.story:
Leeds extended their unbeaten start to the season but had to settle for a point from a goalless draw with much-improved Crystal Palace at Elland Road.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin spurned Leeds' best chance when firing straight at Palace goalkeeper Walter Benítez in the second half after visiting defender Tyrick Mitchell was denied a winner by VAR.

These are heady times at Leeds after they climbed up to third in the table last week after dismantling Newcastle 4-1 and although they are only five games into their second season back in the top flight, expectation was high among fans before kick-off.

But Palace turned in one of their best displays of the season and will consider themselves unlucky to have secured only one point after creating the better chances.

Given Palace had conceded more goals - 11 - than any other side in the top flight this season, it was no surprise they sat deep when out of possession in the early exchanges.

But they were dangerous on the counter-attack and it took a superb recovery tackle from Tarik Muharemovic to deny Jorgen Strand Larsen, while Leeds squandered early pressure with poor set-piece deliveries.

James Trafford was the first goalkeeper forced into a save when diving low to hold Daichi Kamada's shot and with Leeds struggling to find an end product, Pierre Sage will have been the happier of the two managers at half-time.

Trafford was at full stretch low down to brilliantly turn away Yeremy Pino's free-kick soon after the restart and Kamada's shot flew narrowly wide.

Palace were then denied a deserved lead when Tyrick Mitchell lashed home after Anan Khalaili's cross had deflected off Muharemovic.

Referee Adam Herczeg, taking charge of his first Premier League game, awarded a goal, but it was ruled out by VAR, who deemed Khalaili to have been offside.

Leeds almost snatched the lead after their let-off as Calvert-Lewin fired his point-blank effort from James Justin's cross straight at Palace keeper Benitez.

Palace continued to pose Leeds problems, with midfield lynchpin Adam Wharton central to their promptings while Kamada's header span the wrong side of a post as the home fans grew increasingly frustrated.

Another timely tackle from Muharemovic thwarted Palace substitute Ismaïla Sarr in the penalty area as Leeds failed to carve out another chance against an organised, water-tight defence.

article.headline: Arsenal battered by brilliant Brighton to end perfect start
article.description: Arsenal's 100% start to their Premier League title defence ended in emphatic fashion as Brighton secured a stunning 3-0 win against Mikel Arteta's dumbstruck side.
article.linkText: Champions Arsenal battered by brilliant Brighton

images.name: Brighton shatter Arsenal's perfect start
images.caption: Brighton shock Mikel Arteta's dumbstruck side 3-0 to end Arsenal's 100% start to their EPL title defense in stunning fashion.

article.story:
Arsenal's 100% start to their Premier League title defence ended in emphatic fashion as Brighton secured a stunning 3-0 win against Mikel Arteta's dumbstruck side.

Arsenal arrived at the Amex Stadium with ambitions of equalling a 123-year club record of eight straight victories to start a season, but that piece of history looked in doubt right from the kick-off, with a rampant Brighton side delivering a masterclass against the champions.

Pascal Gross blasted Brighton ahead after 31 minutes before Charalampos Kostoulas doubled the hosts' lead on the stroke of half-time.

Arteta sprinted down the tunnel in the hope of masterminding a half-time speech which would revive his side's fortunes.

But Brighton remained on top after the interval and they served Arsenal a dose of their own medicine when Chema Andrés headed home from a corner shortly before the hour mark.

A disjointed Arsenal were never at the races and Arteta will now have 21 days to stew over a shock result, which will abruptly end any suggestion of his side cantering to a second league title in as many seasons.

For Brighton, surely the best result of manager Fabian Hurzeler's career - just days after a brilliant Carabao Cup comeback win at Manchester United - catapults them up to third in the table, just two points off the Gunners.

Arteta might have rotated his side for their win at Ipswich earlier in the week, but here he fielded his strongest side - one that simply could not live with their inspired opponents.

After just seven minutes Bruno Guimaraes, making his first Premier League start for his new employers, gave the ball away, and Kostoulas tried his luck from range.

David Raya got fingertips to the Brighton man's shot, but it was a sign of things to come.

Arsenal were pegged in by the relentless Seagulls and the hosts' deserved breakthrough arrived.

Gabriel and Riccardo Calafiori allowed Gross far too much time to shoot and his fine 20-yard strike pinged in off Raya's near post.

A case could be made for Raya being Arsenal's MVP last season, but the Spaniard should have done better to divert Gross' long-range strike away from danger.

The largely anonymous Bukayo Saka fluffed his lines when he failed to get any meaningful contact on a fine Arsenal counter-attack and Brighton raced straight up the other end to increase their advantage.

Calafiori was out of position and, when the ball fell to Kostoulas, the visitors failed to put any pressure on the Greece forward. He unleashed an unstoppable low strike from 22 yards and Raya was beaten again.

It was virtually the last kick of the first half and Arteta sprinted for the dressing room ahead of a pivotal team-talk, with Arsenal's 100% record hanging in the balance, and then some.

And Andres all but ended any hope of a comeback when he leapt unmarked from a corner to head a third for Brighton with 57 minutes on the clock.

Brighton went in search of a fourth and they nearly had it when Pascal Struijk's header, again from a corner, dropped just wide of Raya's post with the goalkeeper swinging at fresh air.

Kai Havertz might have landed a consolation for Arsenal in the closing stages, but Bart Verbruggen was equal to the one-on-one -- the keeper's only real test of the match -- while substitute Matt O'Riley could have marked a match to celebrate Brighton's 125-year anniversary with a fourth, but Raya was on hand to spare any further embarrassment.

article.headline: Alexander Isak winner for Liverpool on Andoni Iraola return to Bournemouth
article.description: Alexander Isak's second-half strike secured Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola all three points on his return to the Vitality Stadium in a 1-0 victory over his old club Bournemouth.

article.story:
Alexander Isak's second-half strike secured Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola all three points on his return to the Vitality Stadium in a 1-0 victory over his old club Bournemouth.

The Sweden international broke the deadlock with his fourth goal of the season in the 57th minute after some fine work by Cody Gakpo in the build-up to extend the Reds' unbeaten run and reward Iraola with a second win.

Isak has now already scored more Premier League goals in their first five league matches than he did across his entire previous top-flight campaign.

Iraola left for Anfield after three seasons with the Cherries, capped off by leading the club to a maiden European berth last season.

He was greeted warmly as he emerged before kick-off, exchanging a hug with his German successor Marco Rose.

Liverpool had enjoyed two more days of rest than the hosts, who beat Real Sociedad in San Sebastian on Thursday night to open that historic campaign with a win.

Rose was forced into one change, with Ryan Christie starting in place of Justin Kluivert, who the Cherries boss revealed pre-match had picked up a knock in Spain.

Iraola made three changes from Liverpool's last Premier League outing, starting Gakpo, Milos Kerkez and Alexis Mac Allister in place of Ryan Gravenberch, Víctor Muñoz and Kostas Tsimikas.

Liverpool had an early opportunity when Florian Wirtz was fouled by Tyler Adams, but the resulting 10th-minute free-kick from a dangerous central position was curled into the stands by Dominik Szoboszlai.

It remained a closely-fought contest but lacking chances for either side until Marcus Tavernier broke down the left and picked out Evanilson.

The Brazil striker tried to flick cleverly past Alisson Becker at the near post and nearly had his compatriot beaten, but the Reds goalkeeper reacted just in time with a low palm.

Bradley Barcola's deflected effort just after the half-hour mark finally gave Djordje Petrovic some work to do, the Serbian saving with his leg.

A second Szoboszlai free-kick a few minutes later went closer than his previous attempt, but an opener remained elusive as the Hungarian fizzed it wide.

The game continued in a simliar vein after the break. An alert Adams spared the hosts' blushes after a misplaced pass nearly proved costly, before Christie poked Rayan's cross wide.

But Liverpool breathed life into the match three minutes before the hour with some determined work by Gakpo to muscle his way down the right. His cross was intended for Wirtz, who could not connect under pressure, but Isak, who was lingering nearby, pounced and swept home.

Evanilson tried his luck with just over 20 minutes remaining, but it proved straightforward work for Alisson, who had just come out to punch away Alex Scott's free-kick.

Bournemouth could not make anything out of their late set-pieces, and remain in search of their first Premier League win of the campaign.

article.story:
Tottenham Hotspur fired another blank after being frustrated by Everton in a 0-0 draw to extend their winless start to the new Premier League season to four matches.

The two clubs had contrasting summer windows with Spurs signing 10 players and committing more than £380 million in transfer fees, whilst a chaotic finish before deadline day ensured Toffees boss David Moyes ended up with only 18 outfield players.

However, the honours were even in north London where Tottenham's bright start failed to translate into clear-cut chances before Everton squandered two second-half opportunities via Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Brennan Johnson to claim all three points in the capital.

A smattering of boos greeted full-time after Roberto De Zerbi's team failed to score for a fourth consecutive league match.

Spurs are 17th and on two points after last weekend's stalemate at Nottingham Forest and Everton remain unbeaten after a third draw of the campaign.

.

De Zerbi shuffled his pack with Dominic Solanke handed his first start and Richarlison was a surprise member of the crowd following a failed move to Vasco da Gama in the early hours of Saturday morning.

Spurs started brightly with Jan Paul van Hecke sending an effort on the half-volley over from Andy Robertson's free-kick before the Dutch defender produced a wonderful through-ball into Mateus Fernandes, but he failed to get a shot off.

After Archie Gray and Omar Marmoush had efforts blocked, Tottenham lost momentum after a break in play and Sávio had to stick a leg out to thwart Dewsbury-Hall for the visitors.

The influence of £100 million midfielder Sandro Tonali started to grow as he chipped over the top for Gray, who was denied by James Garner before the Italian midfielder let fly from range and had a shot deflect over.

However, Everton had the first shot on target when Garner's stoppage-time free-kick was tipped around a post by Antonín Kinsky.

Everton started the second half strongly and Theirno Barry should have done better when Kinsky failed to gather Tyrique George's cross, but the forward's header hit the face of the Spurs goalkeeper in the 50th minute.

Moments later and Barry should have played through to former Tottenham forward Johnson, but went to his left to George and his cross to the far post was cleared by Micky van de Ven.

De Zerbi had seen enough and introduced Lucas Bergvall, Mohammed Kudus and Mathys Tel but Everton almost took the lead when Kinsky's pass was cut out by Dewsbury-Hall, but his effort was saved by the Spurs goalkeeper.

The hosts remained dominant in possession but Johnson almost came back to haunt his old club in the 75th minute, only to side-foot over from Dewsbury-Hall's cut back.

It was a guilt-edged chance and James Maddison's arrival sparked more belief in the Tottenham faithful.

Tonali had another shot blocked from range before Gray headed over and Spurs' best moment arrived a minute from time when Savio found Lucas Bergvall, but his curled 22-yard effort was tipped wide by Jordan Pickford.

article.headline: Brighton keep pressure on Man City, Arsenal with 2-0 Sunderland win
article.description: Maxim De Cuyper and Jaouen Hadjam were both on the scoresheet as 10-man Brighton clinched a 2-0 win over Sunderland at the Stadium of Light.

article.story:
Maxim De Cuyper and Jaouen Hadjam were both on the scoresheet as 10-man Brighton clinched a 2-0 win over Sunderland at the Stadium of Light.

The game suddenly sparked into life with a chaotic four-minute period early in the second half which saw De Cuyper put the Seagulls ahead before they were reduced to 10 in the 57th minute when Pascal Struijk was sent off following a VAR review for denying a goalscoring opportunity.

Sunderland struggled to take advantage of their extra man and were punished by a Brighton break, finished by Hadjam in the third minute of stoppage time.

A hard-earned three points keeps the Seagulls in the top four, while the Black Cats now linger just above the relegation zone.

Regis Le Bris made three switches to the team beaten 5-3 by Manchester City before the international break as Trai Hume, Reinildo Mandava and Wilson Isidor all lined up, while Brighton remained unchanged from their last outing, a 3-0 win over Arsenal.

Robin Roefs was called into action early on when a loose touch from Kevin Danso allowed Diego Gómez to pounce on the ball and charge forward, but his shot was smothered by the Sunderland goalkeeper.

He made another intervention to tip away an inswinging corner from De Cuyper and Yasin Ayari blasted wide from outside the area as Brighton strengthened their grip.

Despite some positive play from the Seagulls, Sunderland nearly went in front when Isidor met a low cross from Enzo Le Fée and the striker's sliding effort at the near post was deflected behind.

A scrappy period saw the hosts almost strike when a good piece of control from Thomas Meunier saw his resulting shot brilliantly stopped by the sliding Ferdi Kadioglu.

Danso hooked away Ayari's teasing ball into the six-yard box before an injury saw Meunier withdrawn for Malick Fofana in the 34th minute.

Fofana was instantly in the thick of the action and crossed to Danso, who looped a header over the bar before Bart Verbruggen was forced to stop Nordi Mukiele's long-range strike as the Black Cats ramped up the pressure.

However, Brighton continued to threaten and Struijk's tame header hit the post on the stroke of half-time.

Roefs brought down Gomez's strike from distance shortly after the restart and Brighton soon broke the deadlock in the 53rd minute. A quick piece of play saw Pascal Gross squeeze a pass through the home defence and into De Cuyper, who placed the ball into the bottom corner.

However, Brighton's afternoon took a twist four minutes later when following a VAR review, referee Tom Bramall showed a red card to Struijk for denial of a goalscoring opportunity after the defender fouled Isidor.

Verbruggen pushed away the resulting free-kick from Granit Xhaka and Fabian Hurzeler brought Lewis Dunk on to help manage proceedings.

Sunderland struggled to capitalise on their extra player as Fofana had a comfortable shot held by Verbruggen and Brighton looked to threaten when Gomez had a shot turned behind.

The Black Cats dominated in possession but could not test Verbruggen and a late break from the visitors saw Hadjam find the bottom corner to wrap up three points.

article.story:
Dominic Solanke capitalised on weak Manchester United defending as winless Tottenham recovered from Rodrigo Bentancur's dismissal to snatch a late 1-1 draw as boos filled Old Trafford once again.

Michael Carrick and Roberto De Zerbi led the bookmakers' sack race odds heading into the weekend, with the Red Devils' five-point return from five games now their joint worst start to a Premier League campaign.

Tottenham's record was even worse having failed to win a match, and Bryan Mbeumo looked set to punish their latest wasteful display when turning to expertly fire home in the second half.

Bentancur's sending-off for headbutting Luke Shaw increased the incline on Spurs' uphill battle, but United failed to beat 10 men like against Manchester City in their last Premier League outing on home soil.

Sandro Tonali was allowed to send over a stoppage-time cross which Solanke glanced home following some woeful defending by Lisandro Martínez, who scored a calamitous own goal against Fulham last time out.

Boos greeted the final whistle, just as they had at half-time, as the Red Devils' wait for a top-flight victory extended to a fourth match as Spurs showed mental strength that should mean their winless run ends soon enough.

All United had to cheer in the first half was rivals City's guilty verdict, with Senne Lammens forced to produce an important third-minute save after his pass was cut out and skipper Solanke had an effort on goal.

Spluttering United continued to invite on De Zerbi's purposeful visitors and Mohammed Kudus fizzed narrowly wide from a Sávio cutback.

Home fans were growing restless, meaning Matheus Cunha's call for further backing irked some. Amad Diallo could have taken away some of the Old Trafford edginess had he beaten Antonín Kinsky on the break, but Carrick's side continued to struggle after that point.

The first half was summed up when comedic Red Devils defending gave Conor Gallagher a chance that profligate Spurs failed to capitalise on, with boos greeting the half-time whistle.

Tottenham continued in careless fashion as Solanke turned over a Savio cross from close range, with a Youri Tielemans goal ruled out at the other end as Cunha cut back after the ball went out.

Both managers made changes in a bid to change the dynamics, including United introducing debutant Carlos Baleba, as play swung from end to end.

Bruno Fernandes failed with an audacious effort and Kobbie Mainoo produced a key challenge to turn a Savio attempt over.

The opening goal felt like it could be vital and it arrived through a rare moment of United quality. Cunha played the ball to Mbeumo, who turned sharply and slammed home a low strike in front of the Stretford End in the 73rd minute.

It was a gut punch for Spurs compounded five minutes later.

Bentancur's overzealous challenge drew a furious reaction from Shaw. The home left-back's shove on the Spurs substitute led to a headbutt and a red card for the Uruguay international.

Shaw was booked along with Jan Paul van Hecke as tensions boiled over between the benches, with Mbeumo bursting through only to be denied by Kinsky as the hosts sought to settle any nerves.

Tottenham appeared to be running out of ideas, only for Martinez to be found wanting when a stoppage-time Tonali cross came in and Solanke got a touch that secured De Zerbi's men a share of the spoils. Little wonder the Argentina international held his heads in his hands.

article.story:
Hull retained their unbeaten home record since returning to the Premier League with an entertaining 2-2 draw against Everton at the MKM Stadium.

The Tigers have returned to the top flight with an unexpected bang, tasting defeat for the first time in their final fixture before the international break at the hands of Newcastle.

Brennan Johnson found the net in the 34th minute but was denied a first Premier League goal for the Toffees following a VAR check, leaving the sides to go in goalless at the break.

The hosts wasted little time after the interval, however, as Joe Gelhardt opened the scoring in the 48th minute following an error by Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall equalised seven minutes later, with Thierno Barry, who had squandered plenty of earlier chances, then putting the visitors ahead midway through the second period.

Hull responded swiftly, though, with substitute Mohamed Belloumi pulling the home team level in the 74th minute.

Hull were slow off the mark in the early exchanges but eventually produced a forward burst of play that saw both Oli McBurnie and then Lewie Coyle threaten before being thwarted.

Gelhardt caused danger with a run down the right in the 22nd minute but his shot was comfortably collected by Jordan Pickford.

Matt Crooks got his head to a corner 10 minutes later, but James Tarkowski cleared and play sped to the opposite end.

Barry unleashed a shot that was gathered by Konstantinos Tzolakis, but the ball rolled from his hands and was fired in by Johnson for what appeared to be the opener 11 minutes before half-time.

But, after a lengthy VAR check, the winger was deemed to be offside.

Gelhardt and Nobel Mendy went close to easing the nerves of home fans with near-misses before half-time but it was not to be.

The hosts did not have to wait long for the opener after the break, though. Sorba Thomas capitalised on a mistake from Maitland-Niles and fed Gelhardt, who coolly nudged the ball beyond Pickford in the 48th minute.

The Everton response was fairly rapid, however, and Maitland-Niles atoned for his slip-up by finding Dewsbury-Hall, who headed home in the 55th minute.

Barry, who had much to ponder after missing two earlier chances, then redeemed himself when he pounced to lash beyond Tzolakis to put the visitors ahead for the first time in the match.

But Hull, who had made a handful of changes, were not behind for long as substitutes Elliot Stroud and Belloumi linked up and the latter got his left-footed shot past Pickford in the 74th minute to secure a point for the Tigers.

article.story:
Jordan Henderson was the unlikely hero as Chelsea's entertainers blew Bournemouth away in a comprehensive and chaotic 5-1 win at Stamford Bridge.

Former Liverpool captain Henderson, 36, scored two and set up one for Morgan Rogers while João Pedro also hit the net twice for the rampant Blues.

Xabi Alonso's side were two up inside three minutes to knock the stuffing out of a Bournemouth side still winless this season.

Their cavalier approach, to simply outscore their opponents, is unsustainable over a season, as evidenced by the three-game winless run before the international break which culminated in a torrid 3-0 defeat at Brentford.

True to form, after going 3-0 up they briefly gave Bournemouth a glimmer of hope by conceding a sloppy goal from a corner.

But further goals from Pedro and Henderson wrapped up a gloriously watchable romp in the October sunshine.

Cole Palmer, fresh from announcing he has signed a new contract until 2034, set the ball rolling when he sauntered forward unchallenged from the halfway line.

He swivelled in the penalty area and fed Henderson, who struck his shot first time in off the far post.

Chelsea attacked again straight from the kick-off and Pedro Neto was denied by Cherries keeper Djordje Petrovic before Henderson found Rogers, lurking on the left-hand side of the area.

The England star's curler took a deflection off the head of António Silva as it looped into the net, with just 149 seconds on the clock.

Shellshocked Bournemouth, who had lost just one of their previous 13 trips to London, eventually managed to regroup and almost pulled one back when Brazilian winger Rayan burst through.

He was denied by Blues keeper Emiliano Martínez, who reacted quickly to also keep out the follow-up from Ryan Christie.

But the Cherries were caught out by another lightning start by Chelsea at the beginning of the second half.

Just 40 seconds had elapsed when Neto skipped past Silva to the byline and pulled the ball back for Pedro to side foot home.

Five minutes later the Blues defence was breached when Moisés Caicedo attempted to clear a corner off the goal-line only to see it ricocheted back off Evanilson and into the net.

But in the 67th minute Chelsea had a fourth. Rogers fed Pep Chavarría down the left and his cross was snaffled up by Pedro.

Henderson then completed the scoring with a superb, curling free-kick to put the gloss on an emphatic victory for the Blues.

article.story:
Kristoffer Ajer's second-half equaliser ensured Brentford continued their unbeaten start to the Premier League season in an entertaining 2-2 draw at Aston Villa.

Keith Andrews' side have now gone six games without defeat to begin the campaign while Villa's wait for a home league win continues but they did register their first point in front of their own fans.

Brentford's lightning start was capped by Yehor Yarmoliuk opening the scoring with his first goal since January. but it was cancelled out when Nicolas Jackson equalised for the hosts just 88 seconds later.

Villa have relied on John McGinn many times during his eight years at the club and he once again stepped up and thought he gave Villa a much-needed home victory with his first league goal of the season.

But it was Brentford's turn to hit back in quick style when Ajer pulled the game level just over two minutes later and ensured both teams took home a share of the spoils.

The visitors made the breakthrough in the 10th minute after Tyrone Mings' stray pass was gifted straight to Igor Thiago, who saw his cross cleared straight into the path of Yarmoliuk who buried a first-time shot past Zion Suzuki.

But the Brentford fans had hardly finished celebrating before the hosts equalised.

McGinn set Villa on the front foot and passed it to Emi Buendia, his shot deflected nicely into the path of Jackson and he stabbed home for his second goal in as many games.

The open nature of the contest led to chances at both ends of the pitch.

Villa thought they should have gone ahead as Johan Manzambi had a couple of efforts, the latter being palmed by Caoimhín Kelleher into the path of Buendia who fluffed his shot into the building site behind the goal.

The Bees went down the other end and forced Suzuki into his first save from Jaidon Anthony's strike from the edge of the area.

Villa should have gone into the interval in front but were denied by a crucial double save by Kelleher. He may have been at fault for spilling Jackson's initial effort into the onrushing Buendia but he did well the second time by sticking a hand up.

The away side started the second half in similar vein to the first period when Kevin Schade's effort brought a diving save from Suzuki.

Brentford substitute Mamadou Sangare handed an opportunity straight to Buendia and he unleashed an effort which deflected past a wrongfooted Kelleher but also past the post.

Mathias Jensen picked out an unmarked Anthony at the far post but he got his header all wrong before Villa Park erupted in the 77th minute as they hit the front.

Manzambi caused problems for the Bees all afternoon and he set up McGinn who saw his effort bounce off Ajer and in.

But, much like the first half, one goal brought another and this time it was Brentford who got the quick equaliser when Anthony fed into Ajer who expertly tucked home.

article.headline: Man United rescue draw at Fulham after own goal shocker
article.description: A comical own goal by Lisandro Martinez saw Manchester United fail to win for a third Premier League game in a row as they drew 1-1 with Fulham at Craven Cottage.
article.linkText: Man United rescue draw at Fulham after own goal

article.story:
A comical own goal by Lisandro Martínez saw Manchester United fail to win for a third Premier League game in a row as they drew 1-1 with Fulham at Craven Cottage.

It was a lethargic, muted display from Michael Carrick's side, who will spend the international break in the bottom half of the Premier League table, though they were spared from making it three losses in a week by Matheus Cunha's late deflected goal.

Their malaise was summed up by the surreal nature of the goal they gifted Fulham.

It went down against Martinez's name but the blame was shared with his goalkeeper, a botched effort by Senne Lammens to shovel away Calvin Bassey's shot with his legs rather than his gloves, then an equally inexplicable and muddled attempt at keeping the defender's pass back to him out of his net.

Cunha too had been at fault, crumpling into a heap in midfield and allowing Bassey to sprint the ball away, though the Brazilian would redeem himself, rescuing his side in the 89th minute with a shot that deflected heavily off David Affengruber.

There could be little arguing United deserved anything more than they got, indeed Fulham ought to have given Alvaro Arbeloa his first Premier League win.

There was plenty here to offer the Spaniard encouragement. Early on, Antonee Robinson moved the ball inside to Gonzalo García who shot wide in search of his second Premier League goal. Martinez hit a thunderous effort from range that needed turning away at full-stretch by Bernd Leno.

The game had been played at a sedentary, almost pre-season pace but burst suddenly into life midway through the half.

United came within inches of going ahead when Cunha got the better of Affengruber near the byline and cut back for Bruno Fernandes to roll a shot against a post.

Lammens, prior to his second-half howler, made three saves in quick succession, the best of them a smart block from Sander Berge. Oscar Bobb then dragged wide from a good position before Leno was needed again to tip away Cunha's awkward deflected effort.

The United goalkeeper had a perplexing afternoon. At times he was keeping his team in it, sticking out a boot to divert Josh King's low shot behind, then later racing from goal to smother as Alex Iwobi went through.

A lovely turn and cross by Cunha found Marcus Rashford, arguably still not looking at ease back at United, who leaned back and leathered his effort into the Fulham supporters behind the goal.

United got themselves into a horrible mess for Fulham's goal. Cunha made a feeble attempt to keep the ball from Bassey, who put the Brazilian on the floor and raced into the box. His shot was tame and straight at Lammens who made the strange decision to bounce away with his thigh, then could not recover as Martinez's pass back to him squirmed into the corner.

Bryan Mbeumo was denied by a flying save from Leno, who also kept out Cunha's curling effort as it bent towards the bottom corner.

Fulham were almost there, then Cunha's shot span cruelly off Affengruber and in past the stranded Leno.

article.description: Abdul Fatawu's dismissal after being shown a second yellow card for diving capped a frustrating afternoon for Ipswich in their 1-0 defeat at Everton.

article.story:
Abdul Fatawu's dismissal after being shown a second yellow card for diving capped a frustrating afternoon for Ipswich in their 1-0 defeat at Everton.

Having gone behind to Thierno Barry's deflected first-half goal, the visitors then had to chase the game with 10 men for nearly half an hour after the winger's ill-judged choice to throw himself to the ground as he went past James Garner.

Referee Stuart Attwell ruled that was simulation and, having been booked in the first half for a foul on Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, dismissed the Ghanaian -- although, surprisingly, that was not the most controversial decision by the official.

Having been alerted by VAR, he ruled out Barry's brilliantly-executed second-half header as Brennan Johnson was offside in front of Christian Walton, despite the goalkeeper being in the opposite half of the goal to where the ball entered the net.

That may have curtailed Barry's celebrations but he still proved to be the match-winner, although whether his diversion of the ball with his chest was a clever piece of quick thinking or just fortunate as he tried to get out of the way of James Tarkowski's speculative 30-yard volley very much depends on which camp you are in regarding the 23-year-old.

He has five goals in all competitions this season so supporters will look at that as progress but he still has many who doubt whether he has the rigour or quality to succeed in the Premier League.

That dichotomy was evident later in the first half when, unmarked inside the six-yard box, he planted a header wide when it seemed easier to score.

Yet the technique he produced to flick a delightful header inside the far post, having found half a yard inside a crowded six-yard box at a corner, showed there is talent there to be unlocked.

His goal extended Everton's unbeaten start to the season without the side really clicking into gear yet but their fifth position in the fledgling Premier League table is a good base to build from when David Moyes does start to get a tune out of them.

And there are signs that may yet come with improving form from the likes of Harrison Armstrong, restored to the starting line-up, and Tyler Dibling, who after impressing in the midweek Carabao Cup win over Wolves, could have had a goal and should definitely have had an assist after coming off the bench.

And of course Barry, who continues to delight and frustrate Toffees fans in equal measure.

- First-month grades for all 20 Premier League teams: A+ to F
- Andy Burnham watches Everton with Canadian PM Mark Carney

In the 11th minute Jack Clark's blind header dropped for Tarkowski to unleash a shot which appeared to be heading wide until it cannoned off Barry's chest.

Former Everton forward Leon Osman had no doubt in crediting the striker with a deliberate action but critics would say he was getting out of the way.

Johnson had missed a much easier chance earlier, while Emersonn and Fatawu both forced saves out of Jordan Pickford, with the latter also testing the England international from halfway.

Everton retreated into their shell somewhat but were re-energised by Dibling, who forced a good save out of Walton but could only watch as Dewsbury-Hall headed wide his inch-perfect cross.

article.story:
Bruno Guimarães and Bukayo Saka helped maintain Arsenal's perfect start in the Premier League with a 2-0 win over Sunderland.

Following a controlled first half, the Gunners were handed a scare 11 minutes after the restart when the hosts were awarded a penalty, but David Raya made a brilliant save to palm Enzo Le Fee's spot-kick against the left post.

A dramatic twist saw Arsenal lead just two minutes later through a fantastic top-corner finish from Guimarães, his first goal since joining in the summer from Sunderland's bitter rivals Newcastle.

More drama followed in stoppage time when Reinildo Mandava was sent off and Saka scored from the penalty spot to cement Arsenal's fourth Premier League win from as many games, while the Wearsiders slipped to their second league defeat.

Sunderland named an unchanged team from their draw at Brentford, while Arsenal made four switches from their midweek Champions League victory over Napoli as Riccardo Calafiori, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Christos Tzolis and Kai Havertz all started.

Arsenal offered an early glimpse of danger when Declan Rice picked out Saka, who got in behind before flicking a tame effort into the arms of Robin Roefs.

Former Arsenal man Granit Xhaka then threatened for the hosts when his whipped free-kick found Dan Ballard, who headed wide.

The Gunners controlled the tempo but struggled to break through the Black Cats' defence and Gabriel Magalhães saw his low strike from outside of the box fizz wide.

Martin Odegaard moved unmarked behind Sunderland's defence before cutting the ball back for Havertz and the forward blasted over, before coming close again moments later with a hooked effort which Roefs tipped over.

Arsenal's frustrations continued as Mikel Arteta was shown a yellow card and Sunderland began to sniff around the visitors' box when Thomas Meunier's strike was deflected behind before Le Fee fired wide.

The Gunners looked to strike on the stroke of half-time when Saka's cross was flicked away by Xhaka.

Sunderland looked bright after the restart as Meunier's effort was blocked and the hosts had an opportunity to take the lead from the penalty spot in the 56th minute.

Referee John Brooks pointed to the spot when Ballard was brought down by Ezri Konsa in the area and Le Fee's penalty was denied by Raya.

The champions suddenly took the lead in the 58th minute when Guimaraes fired a superb strike from outside of the area, which crashed off the underside of the crossbar and into the net.

The visitors nearly caught Sunderland on the break when Odegaard played in Saka, who was denied by Roefs and Ballard made a goal-line clearance from the resultant corner.

Guimaraes curled an effort jsut wide and the Black Cats then had a promising opportunity when Nordi Mukiele's backheeled effort was blocked.

Jurrien Timber's header from a free-kick was ruled out for offside and Mukiele came close again for Sunderland, hooking a strike over before having another effort saved by Raya.

Late drama followed when Reinildo was shown a second yellow card at the death and Saka slotted home from the penalty spot in the seventh additional minute to seal three points.

article.story:
Uncertainty may surround Manchester City's future but nothing changed for them on the pitch as the Premier League leaders successfully came through their first public examination since being found guilty on breaches of the league's financial rules by an independent commission.

Having been subjected to a febrile atmosphere at Anfield where they were labelled cheats and booed at every opportunity Enzo Maresca's side shrugged off the slurs relating to the numerous breaches of financial rules to win 3-0.

The way they brushed off the taunts was similar to the way the club, who have lodged an appeal, have treated the decision of the independent commission and the fact it was business as usual showed there appears to be no visible concerns from the players when it comes to delivering on the pitch.

Erling Haaland made the crucial breakthrough in front of his father Alfe-Inge -- stood with the away fans waving their throwback inflatable yellow bananas --  just three minutes after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off for a second bookable offence, both soft yellow cards.

Subsitute Jérémy Doku, who helped turn the game the visitors' way after coming on in the 56th minute, curled home a second and Rayan Cherki rolled in a third to allow Maresca the luxury of resting Haaland with 10 minutes remaining with their first back-to-back league wins at Anfield since January 1953 safely secured.

Liverpool fans have reason more than most to feel aggrieved at City's sham contracts which allowed them to inject £830 million of inflated income over nine seasons, having been beaten to the title three times by their north-west rivals.

The resumption of the Premier League allowed them first go at venting their fury but they will not be the last.

But abuse from the stands will not derail this team, who have no association with that period. That will come in the form of a Premier League punishment should their appeal fail.

City would not have relished the trip to a ground where their record is the worst but their opponents were weakened by the absence of Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo, and dealt another blow when Dominik Szoboszlai was ruled out with a hamstring problem.

There was not a great deal of football played in the first half but a huge amount of energy expended as the home side's high tempo pressed the life out of City with Lewis Koumas, on his full Premier League debut, and Víctor Muñoz particularly effective.

Marc Guéhi had a testing time against both and when Rúben Dias hauled Koumas to the ground a scuffle ensured between Alexis Mac Allister and Elliot Anderson.

Liverpool's dominance of the first half - City did not have a shot until the 35th minute - began to evaporate after the break after Koumas and Gravenberch had shots parried by Gianluigi Donnarumma and Mac Allister fired wide in the space of a minute.

A dangerous Antoine Semenyo cross was cleared by Milos Kerkez before Haaland's first sight of goal, with only Alisson Becker to beat, saw the striker roll his shot wide.

But the dismissal of Gravenberch after clumsily catching the heels of Doku proved pivotal. While Liverpool waited to send on a like-for-like replacement in Trey Nyoni, one swing of Haaland's left foot effectively decided the contest.

Doku and Cherki ensured Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola's first defeat was a painful one.

article.headline: Ipswich score two late goals to claim dramatic victory against Fulham
article.description: Ipswich produced a dramatic turnaround to beat Fulham 2-1 after late goals by Abdoul Ouattara and Dara O'Shea extended Alvaro Arbeloa's winless start to six Premier League matches.
article.linkText: Ipswich bag late dramatic victory against Fulham
article.story:
Ipswich produced a dramatic turnaround to beat Fulham 2-1 after late goals by Abdoul Ouattara and Dara O'Shea extended Alvaro Arbeloa's winless start to six Premier League matches.

Former Real Madrid boss Arbeloa had been on course to toast a maiden league victory in charge of the Cottagers after Ryan Sessegnon's sweet 55th-minute strike put the visitors ahead.

It would have eased the pressure on Arbeloa, but the Spaniard watched his team collapse with Ouattara producing a spectacular 30-yard equaliser with two minutes left before Town skipper O'Shea headed home in stoppage time to spark wild celebrations at Portman Road.

Fulham will spend another week in the relegation zone with only two points from six league games and they are now seven points behind Ipswich.

A third win of the campaign for Gary O'Neil's men has them up to ninth in the table.

Winless Fulham started on the back foot but survived two early corners before bright Ipswich attacker Julio Enciso curled wide from outside the area.

The visitors' lackadaisical approach on the ball kept causing self-inflicted problems and captain Calvin Bassey called for calm midway through, which was followed by Arbeloa's young team slowly starting to gain a foothold.

With Josh King's influence growing, Fulham could have broken the deadlock in the 22nd minute but David Affengruber headed over from a fine Alex Iwobi cross.

Sessegnon sent an effort wide shortly afterwards before Sander Berge smashed a free-kick into the wall and Shea Charles sent the follow-up off target.

A lack of quality was evident but Berge's next effort was pushed over by Christian Walton in the Ipswich goal before £34million forward Gonzalo García lashed wide after a slick attack led by King.

Town had the first effort after a goalless first half only for Leif Davis to lift his free-kick high into the stand before Fulham had two penalty appeals waved away.

Garcia was incensed after he had a shot blocked on the line by Issa Diop's arm after excellent play by King, but the ex-Fulham defender had his arm in a natural position.

However, remonstrations from the away side turned into celebrations when from the resulting corner, Sessegnon controlled Diop's clearance and rifled the ball into the bottom corner from 25 yards.

Three minutes later both teams squandered chances with Emersonn heading against a post from six yards for Ipswich after a wonderful Enciso cross before Oscar Bobb blazed over.

O'Neil reacted with Jack Clarke, Chuba Akpom and Zian Flemming introduced and the hosts were furious when Daizen Maeda went down after contact by Sessegnon, but referee Lewis Smith and the VAR rejected penalty appeals in the 75th minute.

When Bernd Leno thwarted Ipswich substitute Sindre Walle Egeli, Arbeloa was minutes away from a first league win but Ouattara produced a 30-yard thunderbolt into the bottom corner after 88 minutes before O'Shea headed home Clarke's free-kick in the first minute of stoppage time.

There was still time for Ipswich goalkeeper Walton to deny Kevin and extend Fulham's winless league start.

article.headline: Crystal Palace come from behind to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1, spoil Oliver Glasner's return to Selhurst Park
article.description: Crystal Palace dealt former boss Oliver Glasner a blow after they bounced back to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 on the Austrian's first return to Selhurst Park.
article.linkText: Palace come from behind to beat Forest 3-1 and spoil Oliver Glasner's return to Selhurst Park
article.story:
Crystal Palace dealt former boss Oliver Glasner a blow after they bounced back to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 on the Austrian's first return to Selhurst Park.

Dan Ndoye opened the scoring in the third minute of what was largely a dominant first half for the visitors, who came to rue their wasted chances when Daichi Kamada drew the sides level with his first Premier League goal in the 41st minute.

Jefferson Lerma nodded Palace into the lead in first-half stoppage time and Yéremy Pino added a cushion just before the hour mark.

It was a first home Premier League victory for boss Pierre Sage, who was appointed following the summer exit of Glasner, the man who led Palace to trophies in the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League.

Glasner's decision to join Forest in the wake of tension between the clubs -- sparked by the legal fallout from Palace's demotion to the Conference League before the 2025-26 season -- came as a surprise to many.

The Forest boss, and returning right-back Daniel Muñoz, were nevertheless greeted warmly on Sunday, save a "you're getting sacked in the morning" chant minutes before the final whistle.

article.headline: Coventry put four past Newcastle to climb out of relegation zone
article.description: Coventry City picked up their first home victory in the Premier League for 25 years with an emphatic 4-1 win over Newcastle United on Monday.
article.linkText: Coventry stun Newcastle with emphatic 4-1 win
article.story:
Coventry City picked up their first home victory in the Premier League for 25 years with an emphatic 4-1 win over Newcastle United on Monday.

The last time Newcastle played on a Monday night they were hammered 4-1 by Leeds and suffered the same miserable fate in Coventry less than a month later.

Jack Rudoni's sixth-minute penalty gave Frank Lampard's side a dream start and their first Premier League goal in front of their own fans since John Hartson scored in a 1-0 win over Sunderland in April 2001.

It was the first time Coventry fans had seen a Premier League goal at the Coventry Building Society Arena with their last goal in the top flight coming at Highfield Road.

Bobby Thomas' last-man clearance left Matias Fernandez-Pardo waiting for his first goal for the club and that proved to be vital as Sidiki Cherif doubled the hosts lead three minutes into the second period.

Newcastle got themselves back in the contest through a belter from Sven Botman after 70 minutes but Coventry were not to be denied as Ellis Simms and Stephen Mfuni ensured they moved out of the drop zone with successive wins to draw level on points with Manchester United on a memorable night.

Newcastle started sloppily which set the tone for their disappointing evening, and it led to goalkeeper Lukás Hornícek giving away a penalty in the fourth minute.

The Czech goalkeeper spilled Brandon Thomas-Asante's routine ball and then brought down Cherif before Rudoni calmly sent him the wrong way from 12 yards.

The visitors settled and looked to respond, winger Harvey Barnes looked lively and collected a pass from Joe Willock before firing straight at Carl Rushworth for their first shot on target.

The Sky Blues had a glorious chance to make it two with their first touch inside Newcastle's box since the goal.

Jacob Murphy's cross was cleared by Milan van Ewijk which set Cherif on the counter attack and beyond a high Magpies line but he could only aim straight at Hornicek.

Newcastle should have been on level terms a couple of minutes before the break when Fernandez-Pardo got in behind the Coventry defence from a long clearance, he rounded Rushworth only to see his goalbound effort blocked on the line by the covering Thomas.

Coventry caught Newcastle cold at the start of the second period too as they doubled their advantage.

A long throw into the box was headed out by Malick Thiaw but only into the path of Cherif who arrowed low and hard through several Newcastle bodies and into the bottom right corner.

The Magpies needed something special to get themselves back in the contest and it came when Botman lined one up on the left edge of the area with a bullet too fast for Rushworth to halve the deficit.

The momentum seemingly swung by the way of the visitors but Coventry somehow managed to restore their two-goal lead.

Thomas-Asante dispossessed Joelinton outside his own box and the ball dropped to Simms who saw his effort deflect off Thiaw and in to make it three after 81 minutes.

Newcastle's night was over, and Thomas-Asante struck the post but it did not stop them from suffering further when substitute Mfuni cracked in a fourth five minutes later, just moments after stepping off the bench.

article.headline: Calafiori, Guimarães help Arsenal come from behind to beat Leeds
article.description: Arsenal struck twice in eight second-half minutes to secure a comeback 2-1 win against Leeds at the Emirates Stadium and move level on points with Manchester City at the Premier League summit.
article.linkText: Arsenal come from behind to overcome Leeds

article.story:
Arsenal struck twice in eight second-half minutes to secure a comeback 2-1 win against Leeds at the Emirates Stadium and move level on points with Manchester City at the Premier League summit.

After a thumping 3-0 defeat at Brighton before the international break, Mikel Arteta's side were staring at a second shock loss in as many matches after James Justin fired the visitors ahead with 55 minutes gone.

However, Riccardo Calafiori drew the champions level when he converted Ben White's header from close range in the 62nd minute, before substitute Bruno Guimarães struck the decisive blow just six minutes after he came off the bench.

Arsenal were below their best against a well-drilled Leeds side, who, prior to today's lunchtime contest, were unbeaten in the league.

But the Gunners' revival here puts their championship defence back on course, and places the onus on City, with Enzo Maresca's side contesting their first match since the club were found guilty of an avalanche of financial breaches, at Liverpool on Sunday.

Arteta challenged Arsenal to use their off-colour display at the Amex Stadium three weeks ago as fuel to torment Leeds.

But it was an hour to forget for the hosts who, in the first half, produced just

Indeed, Arteta's men had only one meaningful effort on goal when Kai Havertz headed Noni Madueke's cross straight at James Trafford.

Daniel Farke's team looked the more likely, and a strong left arm from David Raya was required to stop Gabriel Gudmundsson from opening the scoring on the stroke of half-time.

"Wake up," yelled one Arsenal supporter as the under-performing champions headed for the tunnel.

Madueke's cut back provided Martin Odegaard with the chance to fire Arsenal ahead six minutes into the second period, but the captain's first-time shot was tame, and easy for Trafford to deal with it.

And at the other end, Raya was back in action as he diverted Ao Tanaka's long-range shot over his crossbar.

A sloppy Arsenal were guilty of giving the ball away on multiple occasions, and the home supporters were growing increasingly tense.

Then, with the second half just 10 minutes old, Justin stunned them into submission.

Raya was unable to claw Gudmundsson's low cross away from danger and an onrushing, and unmarked Justin, blasted the ball into the net.

Viktor Gyökeres, Guimaraes and Jurriën Timber were all being readied by Arteta on the touchline with Arsenal in desperate need of a creative spark before Calafiori handed the Spaniard a lifeline.

White headed Madueke's curling cross back across the box and left-back Calafiori was on hand to prod the ball past Trafford from close range.

Suddenly, having been so laboured, Arsenal's tails were up, and just eight minutes later, they were leading the fixture.

Odegaard played in Declan Rice and the England midfielder's sumptuous flick was rattled home by Guimaraes - his second goal for his new employers after joining from Newcastle for £75million.

It would prove the knockout blow as Arsenal saw out a possible crisis to take all three points which leaves them trailing under-fire City only on goal difference.

article.headline: Drab Tottenham fall to Aston Villa loss despite ending goalless run
article.description: Aston Villa piled the pressure on big-spending Tottenham and Roberto De Zerbi with a 3-2 away victory to claim a first win in the Premier League this season.
article.linkText: Drab Tottenham fall to Aston Villa defeat

article.story:
Aston Villa piled the pressure on big-spending Tottenham and Roberto De Zerbi with a 3-2 away victory to claim a first win in the Premier League this season.

Both clubs had made slow starts to the new campaign after summer rebuilds and while Spurs had failed to score in four league fixtures, there had been green shoots in 0-0 draws with Nottingham Forest and Everton.

However, Tottenham's latest strong opening was again followed by a meek collapse after Johan Manzambi broke the deadlock in first-half added-time when he tapped in Boubacar Kamara's cross.

It occurred with Spurs captain Micky van de Ven off the pitch receiving treatment, but boss De Zerbi watched the hosts produce a disjoined second-half performance and conceded again in the 67th minute through Nicolas Jackson.

A superb long-range strike by Emi Buendia with 11 minutes left made the points safe for Unai Emery's Villa before Conor Gallagher ended Tottenham's league goal drought with a close-range finish after 87 minutes.

Jan Paul van Hecke headed a second late on but this latest defeat was greeted with boos, with patience starting to wear thin after a summer of lavish spending.

article.headline: Coventry claim first Premier League win of season at Nottingham Forest
article.description: Jay DaSilva fired Coventry to their first Premier League win in 25 years as they beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 in another game mired by VAR controversy.
article.linkText: Coventry claim first PL win of season at Forest
article.story:
Jay DaSilva fired Coventry to their first Premier League win in 25 years as they beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 in another game mired by VAR controversy.

Frank Lampard's side have endured a tough return to the top flight, with four defeats and no goals, but they put that right at the fifth attempt at the City Ground on a memorable night.

DaSilva's second-half strike ended their drought and proved enough for a first three points in the top division since the Sky Blues beat Sunderland back in April 2001.

Forest thought they had found a late leveller when Igor Jesus slotted home, but referee Jared Gillett was sent to the monitor by VAR and ruled there was a foul on Caleb Yirenkyi, despite his original on-field decision being a goal.

It left Forest with a burning sense of injustice but, in truth, they did not do enough to take anything from the game.

They are having trouble at the City Ground, having won there just once in the league in front of their own fans since December last year.

The VAR decision means Oliver Glasner's men have yet to score in their first three home games, and it is undermining promising away form where they have taken four points from trips to Liverpool and Aston Villa.

After winning at Villa Park last week, Forest were full of confidence and were straight on the attack, with James McAtee shooting straight at Carl Rushworth from distance after just 50 seconds.

McAtee had another goalbound shot blocked as the Forest attacks kept on coming, with Dan Ndoye unable to finish a nice move by curling just over from 18 yards in the 18th minute.

Liam Delap also had an effort from distance that hit the side-netting as Forest probed without creating anything.

Glasner's men were on the front foot again early in the second half as McAtee had a third effort of the day.

Ndoye and Delap combined down the left, with the striker teeing up the former Manchester City midfielder, but his shot was superbly blocked by Ethan Pinnock.

That proved pivotal as Coventry got a foothold in the game, with Loum Tchaouna shooting straight at Matz Sels.

But Coventry's patient fans finally got their moment 10 minutes into the second half as DaSilva broke their duck.

He raced on to Carl Rushworth's long kick, beat Daniel Munoz, and then fired home in front of the jubilant supporters.

Forest had little in the way of an immediate response as frustrations began to grow.

They began to up the ante in the final 15 minutes and almost levelled when substitute Jesus was denied

by Bobby Thomas' acrobatic clearance off the line.

They had the ball in the back of the net in the 86th minute as Jesus took advantage of a slip by Yirenkyi to roll home.

But for the second home match in a row VAR got involved, with Gillett changing his decision after viewing the monitor and ruling Jesus had clipped the Coventry defender's ankle.

article.story:
Chelsea's winless run in the Premier League stretched to three matches as Brentford ran out deserved 3-0 winners at the Gtech Community Stadium.

It was a puzzling display for Xabi Alonso to ponder after watching his team impose themselves on the hosts in the first half yet struggling to find a goal threat, before succumbing in the second period to goals from Jaidon Anthony, Igor Thiago and Fábio Carvalho.

This was a Chelsea lineup containing all the elements of their summer transfer rethink with a solid experienced spine which saw Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck make first Premier League starts.

Something appeared to have clicked. They did not look half as chaotic defensively in the first half as they have done at times this season, standing up physically to Brentford, winning duels and not allowing Keith Andrews' side to dominate second balls.

Yet old habits had followed the visitors on their short trip across west London. The marking from Mikkel Damsgaard's 61st-minute corner was poor, Jannik Schuster headed on and Anthony finished it off, then Thiago was left free to score after Kevin Schade's shot was saved.

It was then a low cross from the German that was whacked in during stoppage time by Carvalho to send Brentford fans into dreamland.

The first chance went to Chelsea, Welbeck showing clever feet and laying the ball off for Pedro Neto, whose drive met a strong save from Caoimhín Kelleher.

The absence of João Pedro was hard to ignore through injury, his replacement Welbeck not quite so able to act as the middle link in a fluid trio with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers.

Both forwards were involved and looked dangerous, but they operated far less in combination than when João Pedro is present.

Yehor Yarmoliuk had Brentford's only real sight of goal in the first half, bursting past the half-challenge of Rogers and shooting low into the gloves of Emiliano Martínez.

The visitors had a new midfield with Valentín Barco in for his first league start alongside Henderson. This was the former Liverpool captain's first appearance of any kind since coming on as a substitute for England against Panama in June, and he was a vocal, commanding presence alongside the Argentinian, who also impressed.

Further up, the Blues huffed and puffed. Rogers was afforded space inside the box to shoot late in the half, but his effort was well blocked by Schuster.

All their good work defensively was undone just after the hour mark when Damsgaard's corner found not one but two Brentford players unmarked. Rising highest to head back across goal was Schuster and Anthony had the simple job of nodding in from virtually on the line.

Another lapse handed Brentford their second goal. Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana were parted by a simple through-ball by Damsgaard, sending Schade clear. His shot was kept out by Martinez, but Thiago was there to knock in his first league goal of the season.

There was a final flourish for Brentford when Schade drilled low across goal in stoppage time and substitute Carvalho arrived to blast into the roof of the net.

article.story:
Erling Haaland secured Manchester City a memorable 1-0 derby day triumph as Manchester United failed to capitalize on Phil Foden's sending-off on a day of contentious decisions.

Old Trafford witnessed a pulsating 199th meeting of the Manchester rivals on Sunday, as Enzo Maresca's new-look side won the first clash between the sides since Pep Guardiola's departure.

Much has changed at City this summer, but Haaland remains a familiar foe, with the striker's ninth Premier League goal against United taking him clear as top scorer in this fixture and sealing City's victory.

But the main subject of debate after the game will be the decisions to send off Foden and award Haaland's winner.

The visitors had felt aggrieved when Foden was sent off in the 23rd minute for petulantly reacting to a Bruno Fernandes kick.

Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo hit the woodwork, but United could not make the most of their man advantage, with the VAR's decision to overturn an initial offside call on Haaland's goal causing anger and confusion.

Gianluigi Donnarumma made a crucial stoppage-time save from Bryan Mbeumo to secure a dramatic win that Maresca celebrated by charging toward the City fans at full time.

Sunday's painful defeat leaves United with just four points from their opening four matches and followed protests about the way the club is being run.

The club's heavy-handed ticket touting investigation has angered fans, who displayed a sign above the tunnel that read "the way you treat us is a disgrace" as Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Avram Glazer watched on.

There was a boisterous atmosphere as fans traded chants, with Enzo Fernández seeing an early shot deflected wide as Lisandro Martínez and Matheus Cunha had hopeful efforts at the other end.

An even clash looked to have tipped United's way in the 23rd minute.

Fernandes caught Foden when he was on the deck and the City star kicked out, with referee Michael Oliver brandishing a straight red.

City players harangued the referee, but VAR Matthew Donohue gave the decision the green light as United fans waved off Foden.

Maresca's side rallied well as United's defense wobbled, but Carrick's side so nearly took the lead just before halftime when Rashford's dipping free kick from distance hit a post.

A frustrated Maresca was booked and his mood nearly darkened shortly after the break when Mainoo curled a fine effort that beat Donnarumma and came back off a post.

United pushed from there. Rashford saw an effort taken into the side netting before Mbeumo and Cunha tried their luck, but this would be City's day.

Patrick Dorgu -- again playing at left back in Luke Shaw's absence -- coughed up possession, and the move ended with a Josko Gvardiol cross being turned in by a falling Haaland at the far post in the 60th minute.

City's initial celebrations were short-lived due to an on-field offside call, only for a confusing delay and award of the goal to change the mood.

The Premier League Match Centre said the VAR "determined that Haaland was in an onside position" and "deemed that while in an offside position, Fernández didn't play the ball."

City nearly added a second goal shortly after, but United goalkeeper Senne Lammens brilliantly pushed Fernández's 20-yard strike onto a post.

United looked limited, with Fernandes, Mbeumo and Harry Maguire trying their luck, as Haaland prodded narrowly wide.

City fans celebrated wildly after Donnarumma expertly denied Mbeumo in stoppage time.
