article.story:
Fulham frustrated Liverpool to claim their first point of the season with a goalless draw at Anfield on Saturday.

Former Liverpool defender Alvaro Arbeloa may feel his side deserved even more after a positive display that suggested a first Premier League win cannot be far away.

Liverpool failed to fire despite fielding their trio of £100 million-plus attacking signings in Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak.

The result left Andoni Iraola unbeaten as Reds boss but with plenty to ponder as he searches for ways to coax better performances from his squad.

They will take the positives from a clean sheet but, until a more sustained spell of pressure late in the game, Fulham were much the brighter side.

Arbeola, who featured in the Liverpool side that reached the 2007 Champions League final, could reflect on a job well done.

Liverpool did have an early chance when Barcola played in Isak but the Swede's shot from a tight angle rolled narrowly wide.

From there on Fulham took control and were unfortunate their energy and creativity did not bring greater reward.

Josh King was particularly lively and had their first serious opportunity when he turned in the area after a good break but missed the target.

Liverpool had a major let-off when Alisson Becker played Ryan Gravenberch into trouble with an ill-advised pass. Sander Berge seized possession and found King, who managed to get a pass away despite a sliding challenge from Alisson.

Gonzalo García fired in a shot but Jérémy Jacquet blocked on the line.

Fulham felt they could have had a penalty for Alisson's tackle on King but nothing was given.

It was the start of a sloppy spell from Liverpool with passes continually going astray while Fulham remained positive.

The momentum could have changed after Víctor Muñoz won a free header from a corner but Bernd Leno clawed his effort away from under his own bar.

Fulham had another opening when King shot at Alisson and Antonee Robinson headed wide from an Oscar Bobb cross.

Isak showed promise after the break when he weaved his way into the area but his shot was tame and Liverpool continued to look leggy.

Iraola had made three changes for the game, bringing in Kostas Tsimikas, Gravenberch and Muñoz, but all three had been taken off before the hour.

One of those to come on, Alexis Mac Allister teed up Dominik Szoboszlai but the Hungarian's powerful strike was straight at Leno.

The hosts tried to lift the tempo and Mac Allister went down in a scramble inside the area but nothing was given and Fulham went close on the counter as King tested Alisson from distance.

With Mac Allister, Cody Gakpo, Rio Ngumoha and Jeremie Frimpong on the field, Liverpool finished strongly as Fulham tired but the visitors held on for a well-earned draw.

article.story:
Leeds sent sorry Newcastle spinning to a 4-1 defeat at Elland Road to extend their unbeaten Premier League start and climb to third in the table.

Daniel Farke's side struck twice in two first-half minutes through Lewis Miley's own goal and Jayden Bogle before Dominic Calvert-Lewin added a third before the interval.

It remained one-way traffic in the second half and Leeds could have won by a bigger margin after Noah Okafor struck their fourth, with substitute Bazoumana Touré scoring a late consolation for the shell-shocked visitors.

Leeds' appeals for an early penalty when the ball appeared to hit the arm of Newcastle debutant Matias Fernandes-Pardo on the edge of his penalty area were unsuccessful as the visitors came under early pressure.

Newcastle goalkeeper Lukás Hornícek was forced into a sprawling low save to keep out Bogle's hooked effort before Magpies boss Matthias Jaissle was forced into a change.

Summer signing Nico González had needed treatment after being struck in the face by the ball in the opening exchanges and he was replaced by Sean Steur in the 20th minute.

Leeds continued to threaten and soon after Hornicek had punched clear Bogle's dipping volley, they struck twice in as many minutes to take control.

Their opener came in fortuitous circumstances. Okafor cut in from the left and teed up Ao Tanaka, whose shot from the edge of the box took a double deflection - off Steur and then Lewis Miley - before spinning into the top corner.

There was nothing lucky about the home side's second though after Steur's misplaced pass out from the back had been pounced on by Bogle.

James Justin's right-wing cross was met by Calvert-Lewin's towering goal-bound header, which struck Bogle on the head before flying into the bottom corner.

Hornicek denied Leeds a third when he kept out close-range shots from Gabriel Gudmundsson and Calvert-Lewin in quick succession, but Newcastle fell 3-0 behind in first-half stoppage time.

Gudmundsson picked out Calvert-Lewin in the box and the striker side-stepped Sven Botman's challenge to fire home a low finish inside the far post.

Leeds were unrelenting at the start of the second period and Anton Stach squandered a golden chance after intercepting Botman's pass.

But after a non-plussed Jaissle sent on Joe Willock, Tino Livramento and Toure for Fernandes-Pardo, Amar Dedic and Jacob Murphy, Leeds added a fourth goal in the 59th minute.

Ethan Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, swung a long throw into the box and Botman's headed clearance was thumped inside the far post by Okafor on the half-volley.

Newcastle had not troubled home goalkeeper James Trafford throughout and a rare shot on target from Toure in the 89th minute was scant consolation for them as they slumped to a first defeat against Leeds in seven matches.

article.headline: Ipswich's impressive start continues with win over 10-man Crystal Palace
article.description: Zian Flemming's first goal for Ipswich snatched a dramatic 3-2 victory at 10-man Crystal Palace for their second Premier League win of the season.
article.linkText: Ipswich beat 10-man Palace with 90th-min winner

article.story:
Zian Flemming's first goal for Ipswich snatched a dramatic 3-2 victory at 10-man Crystal Palace for their second Premier League win of the season.

The Eagles played the majority of the contest at Selhurst Park a man light following Axel Disasi's red card in the first half, as they fell to their third loss in four league games following an absorbing contest.

Jorgen Strand Larsen had deservedly drawn them level to cancel out the hugely influential Leif Davis' header just ahead of half-time before Flemming's late intervention ended the Tractor Boys' run of two straight defeats.

Goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen almost had another difficult moment early in his Ipswich career when he passed straight to Adam Wharton 30 yards out, but the midfielder scuffed the ball right back to the relieved Dutchman.

But Palace were ahead after 14 minutes when Daichi Kamada received the ball in space in the centre and moved it right for Anan Khalaili, with the Israeli's first goal in English football taking a slight deflection off Davis on its way in.

Khalaili almost turned provider three minutes later when his long pass put Strand Larsen in behind, with Scherpen required to beat away his half-volley.

Completely against the run of play, Ipswich equalised in the 23rd minute when Davis swung in a cross from the left and Emersonn was left unmarked to head in his second goal for the Tractor Boys.

The match took another turn towards the visitors when the Eagles were reduced to 10 men on 34 minutes when Disasi was shown a straight red card for a dangerous, studs-up tackle on Jack Clarke.

Ipswich made the most of their one-man advantage to take the lead in the 45th minute when Dara O'Shea's cross was flicked on by Emersonn and Davis arrived around the back to head past Walter Benítez.

The Tractor Boys pressed to add to their lead against their depleted opponents early in the second half, with Clarke having a shot saved by Benitez at his near post.

Palace found a second wind, though, as Quinten Timber battled his way into the area before shooting at Scherpen, with the crowd responding accordingly to their teams' renewed vigour.

It brought an equaliser in the 75th minute when Kamada played the ball into the area for Strand Larsen, who turned away from Issa Diop before shooting across Scherpen into the bottom corner.

The Eagles almost went ahead four minutes later when Scherpen's flap from Will Hughes' cross fell for Khalaili who blazed over from six yards out.

Instead, it was Ipswich who snatched all three points in the 90th minute as Davis' header from Julio Enciso's cross looped against the bar and substitute Flemming forced in the rebound.

article.story:
Brighton dealt 10-man Coventry a crushing 5-0 defeat to condemn them to a fourth straight Premier League loss.

The Sky Blues have lost those games without scoring a goal and remain the only side in the league still to pick up a point.

Both teams took it in turns to have their share of chances in an entertaining first period which featured 21 shots -- the most in any first half of a Premier League game this season.

But it was Charalampos Kostoulas who made his effort count when he put the away side in front with his first league goal since January to give Brighton a half-time lead.

Coventry's afternoon went from bad to worse within nine minutes of the second period as Malick Yalcouyé doubled Brighton's lead before Taiwo Awoniyi saw red for an elbow on Maxim De Cuyper.

Brighton flexed their muscles as Pascal Gross' penalty made it three, Lewis Dunk thumped home an effort from 25 yards and Yasin Ayari capped off a five-star Seagulls performance.

The visitors started on the front foot and shoot on sight seemed to be the message inside the first 15 minutes, encapsulated by Olivier Boscagli trying his luck from his own half. Carl Rushworth did not need to worry about the speculative effort.

Brighton were showing their confidence, Yalcouyé and Kostoulas both failing to work Rushworth.

The hosts tried to show what they had at the top end of the pitch themselves and got their first effort on goal when Ephron Mason-Clark scuffed a shot into the hands of Bart Verbruggen before Jack Rudoni saw a header skim the crossbar.

Coventry grew into the contest and Brighton needed Verbruggen to stop a couple of volleys from Rudoni and Frank Onyeka.

Just as it looked like Coventry had established a foothold in the game, Brighton broke the deadlock in the 35th minute when Kostoulas latched on to a header from Gross and took a couple of neat touches before firing low and hard into the bottom left corner.

Brighton doubled their advantage six minutes after the break when Yalcouyé beat two defenders before racing through on goal and slotting past Rushworth.

Coventry were forced to play the majority of the second half with a man less after Awoniyi caught De Cuyper with a flailing elbow, which referee Tony Harrington deemed dangerous enough for a red card.

The home side's afternoon got worse when Bobby Thomas brought down Kostoulas inside the area and Gross slotted away the resulting penalty.

Brighton's outstanding day, in contrast, got better and better as Dunk decided to let fly from 25 yards with a strike which flew into the top left corner.

There was still time for the away side to get a fifth, Ayari trying his luck from range with a lovely curling effort which once again beat Rushworth.

article.story:
Chelsea's chaotic start to life under Xabi Alonso continued with an entertaining 2-2 draw against Hull at Stamford Bridge.

It was a pattern that has become familiar in the early weeks of the season as the home side took the lead early on through Morgan Rogers and appeared to be cruising until another defensive implosion saw them give up command of the game and gift two goals to Hull's Mohamed Belloumi.

The first came after 28 minutes when Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato each failed to take control of what should have been a simple mop-up job, allowing the Algerian winger to hammer in his first Premier League goal.

Emiliano Martínez then failed to deal with a corner and Belloumi drilled in via a deflection to put Sergej Jakirovic's side on course for another upset at half-time.

Chelsea tottered having again chucked away control of a match before their attacking prowess finally came to the fore once more to stave off an embarrassing home defeat.

Cole Palmer was again their saviour. He found space to dig out a cross for João Pedro to rifle home midway through the second half and spare Alonso's blushes.

Chelsea kept up their useful habit of scoring early. After seven minutes, Palmer fed Pedro, who swivelled and moved the ball to Rogers in space on the left. It was then far too simple a matter of Rogers skipping around Regan Slater and drilling beyond Konstantinos Tzolakis at his near post.

It took just one Hull attack for Chelsea's vulnerabilities to be exposed.

Gusto was hesitant in dealing with a long ball into the corner, then made a feeble attempt to prevent Ryan Giles from hoisting it into the box. Hato seemed not to know whether to attack the ball or to drop. He did neither and, as the ball bounced over him, Belloumi arrived to thump in the equaliser.

Only a good low stop from Martinez kept Giles from giving Hull the lead, but again Chelsea's defensive shape was awful. They would be made to pay almost immediately.

Semi Ajayi headed the resulting corner against the bar with Martinez flailing and the ball came out to Belloumi, whose driven effort was deflected in.

Chelsea had by now let in 12 goals in Alonso's five-and-a-half matches in charge.

Equally alarming was that frailties at the back appeared to be undermining efforts elsewhere on the pitch. The midfield became a wild free for all and the fluidity in attack turned to misplaced passes seeking out mistimed runs.

Reece James' free-kick hit a post as Chelsea rallied in the second half.

Hull then lost Nobel Mendy following a clash of heads as he bravely prevented a certain goal for Pedro at the back post.

Martinez, signed to bring an end to the Blues' goalkeeping headache, spilled a straightforward shot from Slater, recovering just sufficiently to toe the rebound away from Oli McBurnie.

It fell to Palmer to drag Chelsea from their hole. It was his run to the byline and cut-back that found Pedro in space to hammer into the roof of the net for 2-2.

Tzolakis denied Rogers, who got in behind from Palmer's pass, then at the other end Martinez dived at the feet of Mohamed-Ali Cho, who should have won it for Hull.

article.story:
Igor Jesus piled the misery on Aston Villa as his late goal snatched a 2-1 victory for Nottingham Forest at Villa Park.

Jesus struck in the 88th minute to earn Forest their first win under new boss Oliver Glasner and leave Villa without a victory in four Premier League matches.

Liam Delap went some way to paying back his £50million ($68m) fee as he fired Forest in front after just 45 seconds of the second half.

Villa briefly rallied and did at least score their first goal of the league campaign when Alysson levelled, only for Jesus to have the final say.

Unai Emery is having to rebuild following a turbulent summer, where a host of key players were sold, but progress is slow as they sit in the bottom three.

The signs are much more positive for Forest as they enjoyed a first victory of the season -- and a first at Villa Park since 1994 -- with Glasner now unbeaten in eight games against Emery.

It could have been so different had Villa taken an early lead.

They must have been thinking they would never break their scoring duck after an unbelievable passage of play, which saw the ball somehow stay out in the sixth minute.

Emiliano Buendía's cross picked out Victor Lindelöf, whose shot hit Murillo's leg and was clawed away by Matz Sels, with replays showing some of the ball had crossed the line.

The Belgium goalkeeper's save went onto a post, with Murillo's clearance then hitting Lindelof and forcing Sels into another instinctive stop.

Forest settled and James McAtee's deflected effort saw Zion Suzuki get down well before Morgan Gibbs-White shot straight at the Japan international when the ball fell kindly to him.

The visitors should have gone into the half-time break in front after Neco Williams wasted a golden chance.

Forest worked the ball well down the right and McAtee teed up the Wales international in acres of space on the edge of the area, but he blazed his first-time shot over the crossbar.

Emery hooked ineffective record signing Nicolas Jackson at halftime in a bid to improve things.

But they got worse as the visitors took just 45 seconds to open the scoring after the restart.

Delap outmuscled Buendia, was allowed to advance on goal and fired a low 20-yard effort into the bottom corner.

Forest were full of confidence and had big chances to double their lead.

Dan Ndoye headed over and then had a goalbound effort blocked after Delap set him up invitingly.

The former Chelsea striker then had the ball in the back of the net again as he finished superbly from Gibbs-White's through ball, but he was in an offside position and it was ruled out.

Villa introduced summer signings Ibrahim Mbaye and Johan Manzambi and it changed the complexion of the match.

And after Mbaye's curled effort saw Sels tip the ball around a post, Villa finally ended their drought.

A corner was played short and John McGinn's cross was glanced home by Alysson -- his first goal for the club.

- Liverpool momentum dented by Anfield draw with struggling Fulham
- Hull continue unbeaten Premier League streak with entertaining 2-2 draw at Chelsea

It was all set up for a home push for victory, but Forest hit back.

Daniel Muñoz and Xaver Schlager headers were saved by Suzuki before the winning moment came with two minutes left of normal time.

Munoz's cross was flicked on by Gibbs-White into the path of Jesus, who stabbed home from close range to seal a memorable victory.

article.story:
Bournemouth boss Marco Rose was denied a first Premier League win after a calamitous mistake by goalkeeper Djordje Petrovic allowed Brentford to claim a 2-2 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

The Cherries were on course for a top-flight victory at the fourth time of asking under German coach Rose when goals from Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier overturned Kevin Schade's opener.

But Schade lobbed his second of the afternoon into an unguarded net to maintain the Bees' unbeaten start following a dreadful pass from Petrovic.

It was the fourth time in as many league matches since the summer appointment of Rose that Bournemouth have dropped points from a winning position.

In addition to Petrovic's howler, defender António Silva and winger Rayan were guilty of shocking misses on another frustrating day for the south-coast club, while substitute Ben Gannon-Doak hit the woodwork in stoppage time.

Brentford move on to six points from a possible 12 following a third consecutive draw, while Bournemouth have just three after failing to capitalise on another largely positive performance.

The Cherries were seeking a first Premier League win over Brentford in the ninth such meeting between the clubs to kickstart their campaign ahead of beginning their Europa League adventure at Real Sociedad on Thursday.

Summer signing Silva should have given his side a seventh-minute lead but he wastefully headed wide when unmarked six yards out from a Tavernier free-kick.

Brentford, who threatened early on through Keane Lewis-Potter, capitalised on a similar opportunity to edge ahead in the 34th minute.

After the Bees won possession deep in opposition territory, Yegor Yarmolyuk delivered a delightful cross from the right and Schade headed home via the fingertips of Petrovic and the base of the right post.

The hosts' profligacy continued as Rayan somehow skied a golden chance over the gaping goal after Bees keeper Caoimhín Kelleher kept out the initial effort.

Brentford's lead ultimately lasted just four minutes. Kluivert claimed the leveller, swivelling to fire through the legs of Jaidon Anthony and into the net from just inside the 18-yard box after the ball broke loose following Kristoffer Ajer's tackle on Evanilson.

Brentford wanted a penalty deep into first-half added time when Ajer's goal-bound blast appeared to strike the arm of the falling Adrien Truffert. Referee Jarred Gillett consulted VAR before dismissing the appeals by blowing the half-time whistle.

Bournemouth resumed in the ascendancy. Kelleher pushed over from Kluivert, Silva headed narrowly wide and Alex Scott lashed over, before the hosts eventually went in front in the 52nd minute.

Silva's searching pass into the area was controlled by Evanilson, who touched the ball back for Tavernier to drill into the bottom right corner.

Having finally gained the lead, the Cherries swiftly surrendered it by gifting Brentford a 56th-minute equaliser.

Petrovic was under little pressure when he received a back pass from James Hill but he inexplicably played the ball straight to Schade, who expertly lobbed into the empty net.

Rayan almost atoned for his first-half miss when he curled narrowly wide before he was replaced for the closing stages by Gannon-Doak after scuffing another opening straight at Kelleher.

Winger Gannon-Doak nearly snatched a winner in the third of five added minutes but his deflected effort rebounded off the left post.
